title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is axiomatizing an abstract 'analysis situs'. Its basic objects are 'figures', ordered by the relation 'is a subfigure of'. The previous page reduces everything to a poset M of irreducible figures, or strata. A figure F is then identified with a closed, i.e. down-closed, subset of M. The family 𝔉 of such subsets satisfies: (a) it is stable under passing to closed subsets; (b) it contains every principal ideal M_{≤x}; (c) it contains the empty set. Two figures are 'compatible' if they are subfigures of a common figure, i.e. if their union F∪G is again a figure.

This page adds a further axiom.

First (crossed-out) version of C3: three pairwise compatible figures F, G, H are jointly compatible, i.e. there is a figure K containing all three. This is a 'pairwise implies global' (Helly or flag-type) condition.

Final version of C3: let F, G ∈ 𝔉. If every irreducible X ∈ F is compatible with every irreducible Y ∈ G, then F and G are compatible.

NB: the converse is trivial. If F and G are compatible, then all subfigures F' ⊂ F and G' ⊂ G are compatible.

Corollary: let F and G be compatible. Then H is compatible with F∪G if and only if H is compatible with F and with G. More generally, let (F_i) be a family of mutually compatible figures with union (sup) F. Then H is compatible with F if and only if H is compatible with each F_i.

Marginal corollary: F and G are compatible if and only if all pairs X ∈ F, Y ∈ G are compatible.

On the next page this yields the reduction. The whole structure is the data (M, ≤, R), where R is a reflexive, symmetric compatibility relation inherited downward: R(X,Y), X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ R(X',Y'). Figures (at least those of finite type) are recovered as the down-closed subsets of M whose elements are pairwise R-related.

In modern terms, this is exactly a prime event structure (causality ≤; conflict = non-R, inherited upward) together with its configurations. Equivalently, it is a coherence-space-like or flag-complex structure, in which consistency is determined by pairs.
errors: The infinite version of the corollary tacitly needs that a mutually compatible family has a union/sup that is again a figure. For a compatible pair this follows from C3 applied to pairs. For infinite families it needs an extra completeness axiom, or a restriction to finite families or figures of finite type; this is not stated here. Page 59 indeed restricts to figures of finite type.

The crossed-out triple version is weaker than the final C3 as stated. It gives finite joint compatibility only by induction. The final C3 (pairs of irreducibles suffice) is the right formulation; the page silently replaces one with the other.

ideas.what: Axiom C3: compatibility of figures is determined by pairwise compatibility of their irreducible members (binary consistency).
ideas.modern_name: Binary conflict/consistency in prime event structures; coherence condition of coherence spaces; flag-complex (clique) condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981, event structures); Berry (stable domains, ~1978–79); Girard (coherence spaces, 1986–87)

ideas.what: Compatibility with a union of compatible figures is equivalent to compatibility with each piece (distributivity of compatibility over sups).
ideas.modern_name: Coherence/finitary consistency; distributivity in coherent prime-algebraic domains

ideas.what: Reconstructing the lattice of figures from (M, ≤, R): a poset of irreducibles plus a downward-inherited symmetric compatibility relation.
ideas.modern_name: Representation of coherent dI-domains / configuration domains of prime event structures

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck's axiomatics of 'figures' for analysis situs independently arrives at the structure of prime event structures / coherence spaces. This means a poset of irreducibles with a binary compatibility relation inherited downward, whose 'figures' are the conflict-free down-closed sets. It is the same structure computer scientists (Winskel, Girard) used at the same time for concurrency and linear logic. The link between this stratified-space 'analysis situs' program and domain theory / event structures does not seem to have been made in the literature.
missed.quote: C3 Soient F, G ∈ 𝓕, telles que ∀ X ∈ F, Y ∈ G, X et Y compatibles. Alors F et G sont compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests reading Grothendieck's 'tame topology' figures as configuration domains, which would link stratified spaces to directed/concurrency topology and coherence-space semantics. It also gives a combinatorial model for his analysis situs.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics itself is elementary. The notable point is that Grothendieck independently isolates a binary-consistency (event-structure / coherence-space) axiom for his figures. This is a parallel apparently never remarked upon, but it is a minor, foundational-combinatorial observation.
transcription_corrections: 'NB L'inverse [?] évident : si F et G sont compatibles, dans [?] toutes des figures' should read roughly 'NB L'inverse est évident : si F et G sont compatibles, alors pour toutes sous-figures F' de F ... et G' de G (id.) F' et G' le sont.'
'Pour que H soit compatible : F ∪ G' means 'compatible à F ∪ G'; likewise 'qu'il le soit à F et à G'.
'soit (F_i)_{i∈I} une famille de figures [-...-] compatibles' likely reads 'mutuellement compatibles'.
In the crossed-out top passage, '{F, G, H} est une hyperfigure [?]' is uncertain; the sense is that there is a figure K having F, G, H as subfigures.
The margin note '(3)' likely refers to condition C3, and 'J' / 'J'' refer to the family 𝔉 (figures) before and after modification.
